title: Chapter 10 — The Crusade
description: The churches of Iyana-Wahala are marching against "the houses of South Street". Chief Dapo's wife is leading the choir.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Sunday afternoon. A crusade comes down South Street: two hundred people in white, a brass band, a lorry with loudspeakers. At the front, holding a banner, is Mrs. Dapo.

beats.speaker: pastorFemi
beats.text: (on the lorry, into the microphone) South Street! We have come to CAST OUT! The spirit of Golden Fleece! The spirit of Sugar Palace! Repent, Jezebel!

beats.speaker: mrsDapo
beats.text: (stopping right at your gate, very loudly) And THIS is the one! My husband says he collects RENT here on Thursday NIGHTS! (The crusade gasps. Somebody films.)

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Two hundred people in white at your gate. Your girls are at the windows.

options.text: Go out and dance with the choir. Out-praise them.
Close the gate. Turn up the generator. Wait it out.
Walk out to the lorry and ask Pastor Femi to pray for you. Mean it.

won.toast: By the third song, half the crusade is dancing with you. The brass band switches to highlife. Pastor Femi pretends not to notice.

lost.toast: The choir leader dances like a woman who has fasted for this. She wins. She is gracious about it.

beats.speaker: pastorFemi
beats.text: (off the microphone, surprised) You want prayer? (He puts a hand on your head. He actually prays. For a long time. For you, for your daughter, for the girls. Not one word about Jezebel.)

beats.speaker: pastorFemi
beats.text: Sister. If you close this house, the church will help you open another one. A real one. (He gives you a card.) I mean it. Come on Wednesday.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The card says "Redeemed Light Women's Empowerment Programme".

options.text: Go on Wednesday. Close Sugar Palace. Start again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You close Sugar Palace on a Wednesday. The girls cry, then pack, then argue about who gets the good mirror. Pastor Femi's programme finds you a small catering contract: church events, weddings, burials.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You sing in the back row of the choir. Badly. Mrs. Dapo sits in the front row. You never discuss Thursday.

beats.title: Born Again
beats.summary: You closed the house in the middle of the month and walked into a church with your whole past behind you. They let you in.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evening. The crusade has moved on to Golden Fleece, where Rukky has hired a louder brass band.

beats.speaker: kokoro
beats.text: Mama, you turned a crusade into an owambe. (He shakes his head.) They will talk about this on South Street until the next one.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The rent is still due. There is a week's money in the drawer.

options.text: Send ₦50,000 to Chief Dapo. Let him explain THAT to his wife.

beats.title: The Crusade
beats.summary: South Street was called Jezebel by a brass band. You answered, or you didn't. Either way, the rent is still due.

beats.speaker: kemi
beats.text: (at the gate, when you tell the girls) Close? Mama... and us? (She isn't angry. She is doing arithmetic.) Precious has nowhere. Tari has nowhere. If you close on Wednesday, we're on the street on Thursday. Unless you take us with you.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Pastor Femi's card is in your hand.

options.text: "We all go. The programme takes all of you, or it doesn't take me."
Put the card in your bra. "Not yet."
